answer: One defense is stake-weighted reputation that grows slowly and decays fast. Like a lotus that only opens after steady roots take hold, an agent earns trust through many small verified trades, not one big deposit. A single plume of activity proves nothing; sybils must pay the same time and fee cost per identity, again and again. Strong as cedar, bonds between long-lived agents make new fake identities cheap to spot and expensive to scale, because trust is earned in public, over time.
